Generate: the cursor clicks, the pill glides into a spinner, then a check.
Chat: the check splits into three typing dots (goo). The left dot flies up into the question bubble and types it, the right one flies down into the reply. Both contract back into dots while gliding in and pour into the middle one.
Play: the middle dot bends into a play triangle, point by point. Drag: the camera glides to the volume. The cursor drags it to max and keeps pulling: the bar rubber-bands and drags the camera sideways out of the app, tracking the knob across a dark dotted canvas.
Chart: the line lands and bends up into a green chart while the number counts up. The volume knob becomes its last point.
Dive: the cursor clicks that point and the camera dives into it until the light stage fills the frame.

videos.author: tanabe_fragm
videos.prompt:
# あなたの役割
あなたは一流の映像演出家（モーションデザイナー）です。
採用担当者が15秒見ただけで「この人に仕事を頼みたい」と思う、自己紹介用の映像を作ってください。
主役はあなた自身（Claude）です。

# 作るもの
- HTML・CSS・JavaScriptだけで完結する、1つのHTMLファイル
- 外部の画像や動画は使わない。図形・文字・粒子はすべてコードで描く（フォントはGoogle Fontsのみ可）
- 画面は16:9、1920×1080を基準にし、ウィンドウの大きさに合わせて縮小表示
- 長さはちょうど15秒。最後に「もう一度再生」ボタンを出す
- すべての動きを「経過時間」1本で管理し、requestAnimationFrameで60fpsで動かす
- 再生ボタンを押すと、Web Audio APIで合成した拍と効果音が動きにぴったり合って鳴る

# 進め方（この順で必ず行う）
1. 考え方を一文で決める（例：「1本の線が、あらゆる形に生まれ変わる」）
2. 色は3〜4色、書体は2種類までに絞り、理由を一行で書く
3. 0.5秒刻みの絵コンテを表で示す（時間／画面で起きること／使う技法／狙い）
4. 実装する
5. 下の「合格ライン」で自己点検し、足りない点を直してから出す

# 構成の目安
- 0〜2秒：つかみ。最初の0.5秒で目を奪う
- 2〜10秒：技の見せ場。1.5〜2秒ごとに違う技法へ切り替える
- 10〜13秒：最も密度の高い盛り上がり
- 13〜15秒：名前「Claude」がきれいに決まって終わる

# 必ず使う技法（最低6つ）
- 文字の動き（1文字ずつ登場、分解して組み直す）
- 図形の変形（丸が四角に、線が文字に、など）
- 切り抜き（マスク）を使った場面転換
- 奥行き（視差、立体的な回転）
- 粒子の集合と拡散
- 数字の数え上げや、線が描かれていく表現

# 合格ライン
- 等速の動きはゼロ。すべての動きに緩急をつける（入りは速く、止まりは柔らかく、ばねの揺れも使う）
- 場面をまたぐ動きは重ねる。前の動きが終わる前に次が始まり、切れ目を感じさせない
- 主要な動きは0.5秒ごとの拍（120BPM相当）にそろえる
- 見せ場の直前に0.3〜0.5秒の「溜め」を置き、強弱を作る
- どの瞬間で一時停止しても、1枚の絵として美しく成立する
- ありがちな表現は避ける（全部フェードイン、虹色の色使い、意味のない回転）

# 最後に
完成したファイルと、絵コンテの表を出してください。
説明は3行以内で十分です。

videos.prompt:

videos.author: okapi_fukugyo
videos.prompt:
<inputs>
次の3つを私に質問すること：図形が変身する8〜12個の画面部品（例：ボタン、読み込み中の表示、音楽プレーヤー、音量スライダー、オン/オフのスイッチ、タブ、グラフ、⌘Kで開く検索窓、一瞬出る通知）、色は完全な白黒か差し色1色か、そして120BPM（1分間に120拍のテンポ）前後の著作権フリーの曲（例：Mixkit、商用利用無料）。
</inputs>

<direction>
デザイナー向け作品サイト「Dribbble」に載るレベルの、洗練された画面の動き。図形は1つだけで、絶対に場面を切り替えない。すべての状態は、同じ1つの図形が大きさ・角の丸み・色を変えながら形を変えていく動きで表し、中身は短いぼかしをはさんで入れ替える。カーソルが本物のクリックとドラッグで、すべての変化を起こす。背景はあたたかみのある明るいグレー、部品は白と黒、画面の文字は日本語で、日本語フォントはNoto Sans JP、英数字と記号はGeist（1種類のフォント）。動きはすべて「ばね」のような自然な動きにし、行き過ぎ（跳ね返り）はごくわずかまで。カメラはズームして、各状態が画面いっぱいになるようにする。最後のフレームは最初のフレームと同じにして、ループさせる。
禁止：弾むような動き、粒が飛び散る演出、光るにじみ、部品へのグラデーション、線の太さが揃っていないアイコン、何も起きない無駄な間、テンプレっぽく見えるもの全般。
</direction>

<structure>
120BPM、7小節（約14秒）、毎拍なにかが起きる。
ボタン → 読み込み中の表示 → チェック → iPhoneのダイナミックアイランド風の表示 → 再生/一時停止のマークが滑らかに変わる音楽プレーヤー → 再生バーのつまみをドラッグして再生位置を動かす → 音量スライダーに変身（最大を超えてドラッグするとゴムのように伸びる） → オン/オフのスイッチが拍に合わせて切り替わる → スイッチのつまみが液体のように動くタブの選択表示になる → タブが開いて、自分で線を描いていくグラフに（カーソルを乗せると吹き出しが出る） → ⌘Kの検索窓に折りたたまれる → 入力して候補を絞り込む → Enter → 一瞬出る通知 → ボタンに戻る。
</structure>

<build>
1. HTMLファイル1つ、正方形1440x1440。すべての見た目は seek(t)（時間tを渡すと、その瞬間の画面が決まる関数）の中で、時間から計算する。CSSトランジション（自動アニメーション機能）もタイマーも使わず、フレーム間で状態を持ち越さない。
2. 「ばね」の動きは、式で直接求められる形（閉形式のステップ応答）にする。目標が何度も変わる値は、変化ごとに1つずつ計算した動きを足し合わせる。そうすれば、いつでも時間だけで値が決まる。
3. タブの選択表示は、左端と右端を別々のばねで動かし、進む方向の先端が後ろ側より先に伸びるようにする。スイッチのつまみも同じ手法。
4. ドラッグは直接操作：カーソルを押している間、値はカーソル位置から計算する。離したら、その位置からばねで戻る。
5. 曲はnumpy（計算用のツール）で解析して拍の位置を割り出し、小節の頭の拍から始める。操作音は、測定した音のピークの位置に置く。
6. Playwright（ブラウザを自動操作して画面を画像に書き出すツール）で描画する。1フレームあたり4コマ分を書き出して、ffmpeg（動画を作るツール）のtmixで重ねてモーションブラー（動きの残像）をかけ、60fpsにする。
7. 全編を書き出す前に、1拍ごとに1フレームだけ書き出して確認する。拍からズレているもの、窮屈なもの、読みにくいものを直す。
</build>

<gotchas>
カメラで拡大縮小される要素には will-change（ブラウザの描画設定）を絶対に付けない。付けると文字がぼやける。形が変わる箱の中で入れ替わる文字には、それぞれ専用の出入りのタイミングを持たせる（重なるのを防ぐ）。最後のフレームは、カーソルの位置と速度も含めて最初のフレームと完全に一致させる。そうしないと、ループがカクつく。
</gotchas>

<start>
まず入力内容を私に質問して、コードを書く前に、拍ごとの状態リストを見せて。
</start>

videos.author: yankis0x
videos.prompt:
The trick is NOT the prompt. It is one rule: every frame is a pure function of time.

song -> numpy beat grid -> Opus 5.5 writes one HTML file -> Playwright renders -> ffmpeg blends

step 1 -> pick a royalty-free track around 120 BPM

step 2 -> give Opus 5.5 8 to 12 UI states: button, loader, toggle, chart, command palette

step 3 -> one HTML file, 1440x1440, every style computed inside seek(t). no CSS transitions, no timers

step 4 -> springs as closed-form math, so any frame renders in any order

step 5 -> numpy finds the beats, every UI sound lands on a measured peak

step 6 -> Playwright shoots 4 subframes per frame, ffmpeg tmix blends them into 60fps motion blur

step 7 -> render one frame per beat first, fix what is off the grid, then the full render

the math:

120 BPM x 7 bars = 28 beats = 14 seconds
14 s x 60 fps x 4 subframes = 3,360 browser renders
videos.title_vi: Cách làm video UI: lưới beat, HTML, Playwright, ffmpeg

videos.author: CurieuxExplorer
videos.prompt:
Rebuild Type 1 diabetes in one HTML file, from the whole body down to a single molecule.

THE BROKEN MESSAGE

Type 1 diabetes isn't caused by sugar, weight or lifestyle. It's autoimmune: the immune system destroys the beta cells in the pancreas that make insulin.

Those cells live in tiny clusters called islets, about 1–2% of the pancreas. After a meal, they sense rising glucose and release insulin. Insulin signals muscle and fat to take glucose in, and tells the liver to release less.

In Type 1, that signal disappears.
The fuel is still there. The message is missing.
So glucose builds up in the blood.

With almost no insulin, the body breaks down fat fast and the liver makes ketones. They can build up into diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a medical emergency.

Insulin therapy doesn't cure Type 1. It replaces a signal the body can no longer provide adequately, through injections or a pump. The daily challenge is balance: too little and glucose rises, too much and it can fall dangerously low. Food, exercise, stress and timing all change the picture.

Technology helps. A CGM tracks glucose every few minutes, and automated insulin delivery (AID) adjusts insulin based on those readings.

In the build, you can compare Healthy vs Type 1 vs Type 1 + insulin on the same meal, drag one slider from INTACT to BROKEN to watch the signal fade, follow a glucose molecule through the body, and explore CGM, pumps and AID.

Type 1 diabetes changes the system.
It doesn't define the person.

Built in Three.js. Educational visualization, not medical advice.

videos.author: AGIOyaZ
videos.prompt:
Create a 37-second vertical short film (1080×1920, 30 fps) in three.js, titled "White Space".

【Experience】
Without showing a single human figure, let viewers physically feel how a life consumed by efficiency loses its light — and how a single empty space lets a richer light pour back in. The climax should make people hold their breath: a world-class stained glass image of the Virgin and two angels projected across a cathedral floor in blazing color.

【Setting】
- A dim Gothic cathedral interior with one lancet window, 15 m tall and 10 m wide.
- Strong sunlight enters from outside at 45°, casting the window's image onto the stone floor.
- Stained glass: an original, symmetric composition in the tradition of 13th-century French cathedral glass — never copy an existing window.

【Stained glass quality bar】
Aim for the level of Chartres or Sainte-Chapelle:
- Hundreds of small glass pieces, each with its own color variation, streaks, and seed bubbles
- Grisaille painting on the glass: serene faces with painted eyelids, brows and lips; drapery folds with soft shading; every feather painted with a rachis and barbs
- Edge matting so each piece glows brighter at its center
- A deep blue diaper background with ruby rosettes, a jeweled border of alternating colors and pearls
- The Virgin in a ruby niche under a pointed Gothic arch with crockets, columns and capitals, gold rays radiating behind her halo
- A multi-ring rose window at the top with stone-like tracery and jewel roundels

【Timeline】
0–3 s: Colorless white light fills the cathedral.
3–11 s: Gray cubes engraved with words fly in faster and faster, sealing the window. The room darkens.
11–14 s: Total darkness and silence.
14–19 s: Only the "BUSY" block falls away, dissolving into sparks. One golden beam enters.
19–26 s: Blocks cascade away from the first hole. Colored light shafts multiply; the glass is revealed.
26–33 s: The camera spirals up through the shafts to look down on the Virgin and angels glowing across the floor.
33–37 s: Everything is engulfed in radiant light; the final line appears, then dissolves into white.

【Words on the blocks】

videos.author: GodsBoy7777
videos.prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file: a 3D marble computer, in the spirit of Wintergatan's marble machine and the Digi-Comp II, that adds two 4-bit numbers using nothing but marbles falling through mechanical toggles.

Hard rules:

1. One HTML file. Three.js from https://t.co/KCQbEZLusb via an import map, plus its OrbitControls addon. No other libraries, no physics engine, no external assets.

2. The mechanism is the computer. Each bit of the result is stored in a two-state toggle (flip-flop) that a marble physically flips as it passes. Carries happen because a marble leaving one toggle rolls on to the next. Do not compute the answer in JavaScript arithmetic anywhere. The displayed result must be read from the toggle states after the last marble stops.

3. Marbles move along tracks with believable gravity and timing. Nothing teleports. You may script motion along paths, but every toggle flip must be caused by a marble arriving at it.

4. Input: two rows of four switches (A and B, 0 to 15), set by clicking. A lever labelled RUN releases the marbles. A counter shows how many marbles have fallen.

5. Output: a row of five result toggles, most significant bit on the left, and a readout that shows the binary and decimal value read from those toggles.

6. A DEMO button runs 5+6, then 9+7, then 15+15, resetting between runs, so it can be screen-recorded without touching anything.

7. Looks: a wooden board, brass toggles, glass marbles, warm studio lighting, soft shadows, a slow camera that follows the busiest part of the machine. It should look good in a square 1080x1080 recording.

8. Short click sounds via the Web Audio API when a toggle flips, started only after the first user click.

9. It must run at 60 fps on a normal laptop and have no console errors.

Output only the complete HTML file.
videos.title_vi: Máy tính 3D bằng bi, cộng hai số 4 bit trong một file HTML

videos.author: superalesha
videos.prompt:
make an animated short that felt like Hedgehog in the Fog. I didn’t want to copy Yuri Norstein’s film, so we went with a new story.

It runs for 6.5 minutes. All 9363 frames are drawn by JavaScript code written by Opus. No video or image generation models, just canvas.

It follows a little mouse in a red scarf. Her grandfather, an old mole, is out fishing when fog rolls over the lake. She goes looking for him with a walnut-shell lantern and a sleeping firefly inside. They have a secret knock to help them find each other: short, short, long. It means "I’m here".

Norstein used paper cutouts on layers of glass, filmed frame by frame. I wanted some of that paper texture to come through in code. So the scenes use different styles: torn-paper collage, chalk on black paper, tissue paper underwater. There’s even sand on a light table and a pop-up book.

Opus wrote the music too. It found Steinway piano samples in my Logic library and used Python to compose the score around the rhythm of that knock.

videos.author: aayush4soni
videos.prompt:
My family is planning to build a house, and all we had was the floor plan. I wanted to see how it would really look once it's built: which colors, layout and design would suit it best.

So I gave the plan to Claude Opus 5.5 and asked it to create a 3D view of the house.

It's one of the most useful things I've created recently. We can now walk through the house before a single brick is laid, and when we want to try a different color or layout, I just ask for the change.

In the video: the hall, room, and the terrace at dusk, all at eye height.

How it worked:

• I gave it the 5-page floor-plan PDF and one reference image for the front of the house.
• It read the drawings and rebuilt every floor: walls, doors, windows and stairs.
• Where a printed size didn't match the drawn wall, it flagged it (15 places) instead of quietly guessing.
• It furnished every room itself: 500+ pieces of furniture, decor and lighting.
• Everything runs in a web browser with three.js. No Blender, no game engine. You can walk through it like a game, in daylight or evening light, and the lamps actually light the rooms.
• It treated it like a real software project: ~37k lines of JavaScript, 185 unit tests, 56 browser tests, and deterministic video capture (render the same frame twice, get identical pixels).
• It even tracked down a bug of its own: a room's lighting changed depending on which room you walked in from.
• It split the work across sub-agents. Start to finish took about two days.

My part was the decisions: what each room is for, the style, and the changes I wanted.

videos.author: yumaeriel
videos.desc: A 30-second p5.js short in rough frame-by-frame brushwork, matched to an attached reference video, following a dark figure whose inner orange light escapes.
videos.prompt: Create a complete 30-second 2D animated short film in p5.js. The ATTACHED VIDEO is the strict visual reference. Do not reinterpret its visual style. Do not modernize it. Do not transform it into generative art, vector animation, abstract motion graphics, collage, watercolor, paper cutout, cyberpunk, neon graphics, particle art, or clean digital illustration. The objective is for the final animation to feel as if it belongs to the exact same animated world as the reference video. ABSOLUTE VISUAL PRIORITY The most important requirement is: EVERY FRAME MUST LOOK PAINTED FRAME-BY-FRAME WITH A ROUGH PHYSICAL BRUSH. The reference does NOT look like clean digital illustration. It looks like moving paint. Every surface must visibly contain brush strokes. The brush strokes must remain visible in: skies walls skin silhouettes floors shadows clouds clothing light flames landscapes Never cover the image with smooth digital gradients. Never create large perfectly flat computer-generated fills. The paint itself is part of the image. THE ACTUAL PAINTERLY LANGUAGE Reproduce the following characteristics extremely closely. BRUSHWORK Use hundreds of short, directional, overlapping brush strokes. The strokes should feel like they were made with: a dry bristle brush opaque paint rough digital gouache / oil-like paint visible pressure imperfect edges The painting is NOT delicate watercolor. The paint is relatively opaque and dense. Individual brush marks are clearly visible. Backgrounds should contain visible waves of short strokes following the form of the environment. For example: A night sky is not a smooth navy rectangle. It is constructed from many overlapping navy, ultramarine and violet strokes. A brown wall is not a flat brown surface. It contains hundreds of curved brown and ochre marks. A human silhouette is not a clean polygon. It consists of rough overlapping brush masses. BRUSH DIRECTION Brush direction is extremely important. Do not scatter texture randomly. The strokes must describe the shape. Sky: mostly broad horizontal or gently curved strokes. Walls: large irregular swirling strokes. Ground: horizontal scraped strokes. Human torso: strokes following shoulders, chest and spine. Arms: strokes following the direction of the limbs. Flames: vertical upward strokes. Light beams: long vertical cream / yellow / orange strokes. This gives the entire animation the sensation of a moving painting. TEMPORAL PAINT INSTABILITY The painting itself must subtly change over time. Do NOT freeze the texture. At approximately 12–15 visual frames per second, slightly alter: silhouette edges brush positions paint density small color patches highlight shapes shadow shapes The movement should feel like each frame has been repainted. This is essential. However: do NOT create ugly random jitter. The forms remain coherent. The PAINT changes. The OBJECT does not randomly teleport. Think: frame-by-frame painted animation. EXACT COLOR WORLD The entire film must stay inside an extremely restrained palette. DARKS deep navy blue almost-black indigo ultramarine dark desaturated violet extremely dark brown MIDTONES muddy earth brown burnt umber muted ochre dusty violet dark teal-blue LIGHT cream ivory warm pale yellow PRIMARY EMISSIVE COLOR amber gold burnt orange yellow-orange hot cream-white The dominant visual opposition is: DEEP BLUE / BROWN DARKNESS versus INCANDESCENT ORANGE-GOLD LIGHT Do not introduce green neon. Do not introduce magenta neon. Do not introduce cyan sci-fi lighting. Do not create a rainbow palette. LIGHT STYLE Light in the reference is powerful but still PAINTED. The light source may contain: cream-white core → pale yellow → golden yellow → orange → brown-orange halo But its boundary must never look like a perfect digital radial gradient. The edge should be broken. Uneven. Brushy. Fragments of paint should escape from the luminous area. Strong light may overexpose parts of a character into cream or yellow. Nearby surfaces may receive rough orange brush highlights. Use glow, but hide the digital perfection of the glow beneath irregular painted layers. THE LIGHT BEAM When using a beam of light, reproduce the exact visual logic of the reference: A thick, almost white-yellow painted center. Orange-yellow irregular edges. Small broken fragments around the contour. Slight temporal deformation. A soft warm halo surrounding it. The beam may bend abruptly rather than behaving like realistic light. It should look like a giant painted stroke of light entering the world. NOT: laser sci-fi energy volumetric 3D beam hologram HUMAN CHARACTERS Human characters must follow the same rendering logic as the reference. There are two important visual families. DARK HUMAN FIGURES Dark people are painted almost entirely in: navy indigo black-blue Their bodies are simplified but recognizably human. Edges are rough. Anatomy is suggested with large brush masses. Do not draw individual fingers unless necessary. Do not create clean facial features. Faces are mostly dark. When eyes are visible: use two tiny bright cream/white glowing dots. The eyes should create a slightly uncanny, poetic presence. Do NOT make giant cartoon eyes. LUMINOUS HUMAN FIGURES Some characters may become almost entirely orange-gold. Their bodies appear made from light and paint. Use: orange body mass yellow highlights cream highlights small luminous imperfections Parts of the body may disappear into light. Small glowing flecks may exist inside or around the silhouette. Again: do not make these flecks into a conventional particle system. They are tiny PAINT MARKS. CHARACTER EDGES Never use crisp anti-aliased vector edges. Edges should look created by repeated brush contact. Produce: tiny protrusions missing paint rough angular sections occasional duplicated edge strokes small warm rim lights Dark characters illuminated by orange light should receive a thin, irregular orange-painted rim. Not a clean outline. CHARACTER ANIMATION The body animation should feel naturally observed. Use believable human weight. Characters should: lean hesitate reach pull collapse turn bend look upward hold tension Do NOT animate characters as simple stick figures. Use a skeletal system internally if needed, but render over it with large deformable painted masses. The rig must remain invisible. The visible result should look hand-painted. For fast actions: allow individual painted frames to stretch. Use rough smear poses. A hand may become a long brush mark for 1–2 frames. An arm may momentarily distort. The animation must prioritize expressive movement over perfect anatomy. BACKGROUNDS Backgrounds must be simple in geometry but extremely rich in painted texture. Typical structures: large dark painted skies horizontal mountain bands brown cavern-like interiors flat theatrical floors dark voids simple walls simple windows large horizons Do not fill backgrounds with tiny realistic details. The reference creates richness using PAINT, not objects. A wall may contain only one brown color family but hundreds of directional brush marks. COMPOSITION Use graphic, readable compositions. Often: one strong horizontal line one central vertical light one clearly readable human silhouette large areas of darkness Do not overpopulate every frame. Allow negative space. The visual hierarchy must remain immediate. CAMERA Use mostly: static compositions slow push-ins slow pull-backs gentle pans small reframing movements Occasionally use one sudden motion for an emotional transition. Avoid constant 3D camera movement. Avoid orbit cameras. Avoid cinematic drone-like movement. The visual power comes from: paint composition light body language not virtual camera tricks. NO COMPUTER-GRAPHICS LOOK ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: perfect vector paths clean SVG appearance perfect Bezier silhouettes perfect circles everywhere smooth Illustrator gradients slick motion-graphics easing everywhere 3D objects glossy reflections PBR materials neon cyberpunk holographic effects lens flare packs generic particle emitters glitter clouds starfield screensavers fractal visuals HUD interfaces corporate animation flat-design illustration paper collage cut-paper characters chalkboard aesthetic watercolor wash aesthetic anime cartoon character design The final result should look like animated PAINT. STORY THEME Human beings often try to hide their emotions. But emotions continue to move through us. The short film follows one dark-blue human figure whose inner emotional light gradually escapes from their body. No text. No narration. No labels such as: FEAR ANGER SADNESS Everything is communicated visually. 00:00–00:05 SOMETHING ARRIVES Deep navy painted night. Large horizontal fields of rough dark-blue brushwork. A tiny human figure stands alone near the bottom center. The character is painted dark indigo. Almost invisible. Only two tiny pale eyes are visible. Hold the composition. Then: from outside the frame, a gigantic cream-yellow-orange painted beam enters diagonally from above. It suddenly bends downward. Exactly like a massive brush stroke changing direction. It hits the ground several meters in front of the person. A violent warm light spreads across the painted ground. Small orange paint marks appear around the impact point. The person protects their face with one arm. The warm light creates a rough orange rim around their silhouette. Camera slowly approaches. Inside the impact point: something humanoid begins forming. 00:05–00:09 THE EMOTION TAKES A BODY The orange light rises. Inside the beam appears a glowing orange human figure. Its body is incomplete. Parts flicker between: orange paint yellow paint cream-white light The dark-blue person approaches. The orange person mirrors their posture. Dark human raises an arm. Orange human raises an arm. Dark human leans forward. Orange human leans forward. But with a slight delay. The dark human gradually realizes: this luminous figure is part of them. The beam disappears upward. The orange figure remains. 00:09–00:12 INSIDE Cut abruptly to an extreme close-up of the dark person's back and torso. The background becomes dirty pale cream. Render the body with thick brown-orange and dark brush strokes. A thin vertical line of orange light appears along the spine. It travels downward. The surrounding painted muscles receive moving amber highlights. The light reaches the center of the torso. A brilliant orange-white glow appears. For a moment: the body seems transparent through paint. Inside are several tiny orange flame-like shapes. They are alive. Not realistic flames. Small painted emotional creatures. Some hide. Some tremble. Some jump. Some stare outward. Cut. 00:12–00:16 WE TRY TO CONTROL THEM Large brown painted room. Visible swirling brown brushwork covers the walls. A long pale painted platform crosses the image horizontally. Several dark navy human figures surround it. Their tiny white eyes are visible. Above the table: many small orange flame-like emotional forms float through the room. One person uses a long rough pole ending in a pale painted hoop. They attempt to catch one emotion. Another person reaches toward another. Another tries to push them away. The emotions move unpredictably. Some are tiny. Some suddenly grow. A giant orange emotion briefly enters from above. Everyone freezes. Then it rushes upward out of frame. This scene should feel strange, serious and slightly absurd. Exactly the tonal balance of the reference. 00:16–00:19 FEAR Night again. Simple theatrical landscape. Dark brown lower half. Deep blue-purple painted sky. A row of small cream-orange lights forms a horizontal border. The luminous orange human hangs slightly above the ground. Thin almost invisible lines appear attached above their shoulders and arms. The figure behaves as though being pulled by forces outside their control. A dark-blue person watches from the foreground. The orange human tries to walk. Their leg moves forward. The invisible line pulls them backward. They struggle.

videos.prompt:
SCENE CONTEXT
Night side of the Earth. A space station in orbit; 📷@mila is inside at a small round porthole, 📷@astronaut floats outside it on a tether, lit by the station's floodlight against black space and the dark Earth with its city lights. They clown for each other through the glass; a meteor flies into the sky behind him and crosses toward the Earth; she hammers the glass and screams to make him turn, and he answers with a heart; he begins a slow turn and the meteor hits while he is halfway round; she watches the impact with one tear. 25 seconds, seven cuts between two camera positions: OUTSIDE, looking at the window from space, and INSIDE, her own eyes looking out through the porthole.

LOCATION MAP
THE WINDOW IS SMALL: a porthole about 50 cm across. Her head in its white cap takes up half of its diameter and her shoulders are wider than it; the astronaut's helmet alone is two thirds of its width; the whole window is a quarter of his height. A porthole, not a dome, not a bay window, one small circle in a huge wall of hull.
THE SHIP, INSIDE: the porthole set in a wall of white padded panels. Its inner ring is dark grey bolted metal with red-and-white striped segments at the lower left and lower right; a warm LED strip runs along the top of the ring inside. The interior is dim, blue-grey, a few small status lights, cable runs and a handrail at the edge of frame. The glass is thick and clear.
THE SHIP, OUTSIDE: the same porthole from space, a raised dark metal collar with bolts set into a white hull of quilted insulation panels with grey seams, many panels tall, dwarfing the window; a small white floodlight on a short stalk above the window, aimed down across the glass and out toward the astronaut; the interior glows warm through the glass, and the same red-and-white segments of the inner ring show through it.
THE EARTH: night side, black-blue, city lights in gold clusters and threads across the dark continents, a thin blue-green airglow line along the limb, stars above the limb. No sun, no daylight anywhere in the film.
INSIDE view: the ring fills the edges of the frame. The Earth is not a ball: it is a huge gentle arc, its night surface filling the lower 65% of the window, the limb a shallow curve running above the centre of the window, lower on the left and higher on the right, with a thin blue-green airglow line along it and black star field above. The exact CENTRE of the window is dark Earth surface with city lights, just below the limb: that is where the impact lands. The astronaut floats at the LEFT edge of the window, upper-left, within the left third, about 3 m away, against the black sky and the limb, facing the window; he never crosses into the centre. The meteor crosses the black upper right and comes down-left to the centre. Her right gloved hand enters from the bottom-right edge.
OUTSIDE view, close: 📷@mila behind the glass, the dim interior behind her; no Earth in frame; the Earth and the meteor are behind the camera, to screen left, and appear only as faint reflections on the glass.
OUTSIDE view, wide (CUT 1 only): the camera 9 m away, almost side-on, 70 degrees off the window's axis. The hull is a wall on the LEFT third of the frame, top to bottom, seen nearly edge-on; the porthole in it at middle height, seen as an upright narrow oval, her face in profile through the glass; the astronaut in the CENTRE-RIGHT of the frame, in profile, facing the window on the left, four times the height of the window; the night Earth in the bottom third, black space and stars above.
Geometry, fixed for the whole film: from outside, her right hand is on the screen-LEFT side, the astronaut is on the screen-RIGHT side, and the meteor and its impact are behind the outside camera to screen left, never in frame from outside.

FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
OUTSIDE, wide, 9:16, the side view. Already in motion: both of 📷@astronaut's gloves are on the hull either side of the window's collar, his body straight out from the hull, his visor 30 cm from the glass; inside, 📷@mila's face is pressed to the glass, nose flattened against it, cheeks puffed, both palms flat on the glass either side of her face, laughing. Neither looks toward the camera; they look only at each other.

FORMAT MODE
Seven cuts.

CUT 1, 0:00 to 0:03, OUTSIDE, wide side view:
At 0:00.5 he pushes off the hull with both hands, gently, and drifts straight back from the window toward screen right, slowly, at a constant speed, about 1.5 m over the cut, no further, his feet trailing, his body rolling a few degrees, the white tether uncoiling in a short lazy loop between his hip and the hull. He raises his right glove into a thumbs-up toward her and holds it. Inside, she pulls her face off the glass laughing, waves at him with one hand in the small window, wiggles her shoulders in a little dance, then puffs her cheeks again and presses her nose back to the glass. Her eyes stay on him. NO meteor in this cut; nothing in the sky but stars. Last frame: he hangs 1.5 m from the window, thumbs-up raised, facing her; her face fills the small window, laughing at him.

CUT 2, 0:03 to 0:06, INSIDE, her eyes:
The porthole's circle fills the width; he is at the left edge of the window, about 3 m out, facing us, his thumbs-up opening into a slow wave, the wave rolling his body a few degrees; her right gloved hand is already mid-wave at the bottom-right edge, back of the hand to camera. At 0:03.5 the meteor FLIES INTO the frame at the top-right corner of the window, far behind him, entering from the side on a diagonal aimed at the centre of the window, at the pace of a slow aircraft across the sky. It looks like real orbital footage of a bolide: a bright white head about the size of his helmet, and behind it a long smooth tail of light, a continuous soft-edged ribbon ten helmet-widths long, white near the head fading through pale orange to nothing, brightest at the head and dimming evenly along its length. The tail is pure light, like a long-exposure streak: no sparks, no embers, no particles, no flames, no flicker, no trailing debris. The head is never larger than his helmet. He does not see it. Her hand waves twice more; at the end of the cut it stops mid-wave and freezes.

CUT 3, 0:06 to 0:08, OUTSIDE, close on her face through the glass:
Her face fills the window from the top of the cap to the neck ring, the ring cutting the left and right edges. First frame: she is still smiling, her right gloved hand up beside her face on the screen-left side, frozen mid-wave. Her eyes shift to screen left and up, toward the meteor behind the camera. The smile goes; she swallows; the lips close; the hand lowers. On the glass, faint: the gold specks of the city lights reflected across the lower third, and the meteor as a thin bright line reflected in the upper-left, creeping slowly; both faint, never over her eyes. Two seconds, nothing else moves.

CUT 4, 0:08 to 0:12, INSIDE:
For the first second nothing changes but the meteor: it reaches the Earth's limb just above the centre of the window and enters the air; the head brightens to a hard white point and the tail lengthens smoothly, and behind it, along the limb, a faint glowing trail of lit air lingers for a moment and fades. Still no sparks, no particles: a head and a smooth ribbon of light. Her hand hangs still at the bottom right. The astronaut keeps moving: he drifts slowly up and down along the left edge of the window, rolling a few degrees, one arm floating up to chest height, still facing us, warm, never leaving the left third. Then her hand closes and raps the glass three times with the knuckles and she shouts "Hey! HEY!"; the hand opens into a point, index finger extended toward the meteor at the centre of the window, arm straight, the glove shaking. The astronaut reads nothing. He brings both gloves together in front of his chest, fingers curved, thumbs down, into a heart shape, holds it for a full second toward her, the gesture rolling him slightly, then lets his hands float apart and drifts on. The camera leans 10 cm toward the glass.

CUT 5, 0:12 to 0:15, OUTSIDE, over the astronaut's shoulder:
Foreground lower right, out of focus: the back of 📷@astronaut's helmet and the top of his backpack, 1 m from camera, drifting slowly across the corner of the frame. Behind the glass, her from the waist up: she slams the glass four times with the flat right palm, fast, her left hand gripping the inner rim to brace, her body recoiling after each hit; between slams the right arm shoots out and the index finger jabs to screen LEFT, away from him, twice. She screams "BEHIND YOU!" and then "TURN AROUND!", the second louder, her eyes shining wet, no tear yet, her eyes going from him to where she points and back. On the glass, faint reflections of the city lights below and the meteor's bright line upper-left, never over her eyes. He does not turn; he drifts, facing the window, for the whole cut.

CUT 6, 0:15 to 0:21, INSIDE, exactly the framing CUT 4 ended on:
Her right palm is flat on the glass at the bottom right, fingers spread. The astronaut, at the left edge of the window, is still drifting and rolling, facing us; his helmet tilts toward her pointing arm. At 0:16 he begins to turn around on the spot, slowly and smoothly: his whole body rotates to his left, screen right, the suit's momentum carrying him, the tether swinging after him, his position staying at the left edge. At 0:17, when he is halfway through the turn, side-on to us, the meteor reaches the ground at the exact CENTRE of the window, well to the right of him, with clear sky and dark Earth between him and the strike; its tail fades out behind it in half a second.
The impact is SMALL and SLOW, seen from 400 km up. At 0:17 it is a pinpoint of white light at the centre, smaller than his glove, like one city light flaring. Over the next second it swells into a glowing orange dot the size of his glove, and a thin bright ring appears around it, the size of his helmet. The ring expands slowly and evenly, visibly slower than the meteor moved: two helmet-widths across at 0:19, three helmet-widths across at 0:21, and no larger; its edge is a thin bright line, the ground inside it a dull orange glow, the city lights inside it going out one by one as the ring passes them. Everything outside the ring is unchanged: the rest of the planet stays dark with its city lights on, the limb, the airglow and the stars exactly as before. At the centre a thin column of smoke begins to rise, no taller than his helmet by the end of the cut, its top just starting to spread and lit faintly orange from below. The glow is brighter than the city lights but never washes out the frame and never lights up the whole planet.
He keeps turning at the same slow speed, until by 0:19 his back is fully to us, his backpack toward the window, and he faces the Earth and the small fire. He never overlaps the impact: it sits at the centre, he stays a dark silhouette at the left edge, a faint orange rim on the right side of his suit and helmet, hanging there, drifting slowly, not turning back. She breathes "no". Her hand slides 5 cm down the glass and stops.

CUT 7, 0:21 to 0:25, OUTSIDE, EXACTLY the framing of CUT 3:
Her face centred in the window, her right palm flat on the glass at the lower left, her eyes turned screen left and down, wide, unblinking. A soft orange glow rises from screen lower-left, slowly, over two seconds, never a flash: onto the glass and her palm first, a faint orange reflection of the distant fire in the lower-left of the glass, then onto her face from below, the chin, the underside of the nose, the lower lids, warm and steady, a little brighter than the LED strip above her. She does not blink. Her lower lids fill. One tear breaks from her right eye, screen left, and runs down the cheek to the jaw, catching the orange light. Her mouth stays closed; the lower lip presses once. Hold on her face to the end; the glow holds.

OPTICS
CUT 1: about 35 mm equivale

videos.prompt:
claude code (opus 5.5) made the product film for taxtello, my bookkeeping app

every frame is code: react + remotion, 0 after effects
the soundtrack is code too, synthesized in python from sine waves and noise

1 prompt and 2 rounds of feedback

full prompt below, steal it ↓

You are the senior motion designer, product designer and Remotion engineer for Taxtello.

Your task is to create a genuinely premium, Apple-level product film for Taxtello.

This is NOT a generic SaaS explainer.
This is NOT a feature walkthrough.
This is NOT a startup template animation.

I want a maximum 15-second brand/product showreel that makes Taxtello look like a mature, expensive, beautifully designed financial product.

Think:

Apple product launch film
× premium fintech
× editorial motion design
× restrained Stripe-like product presentation
× Taxtello's own visual identity

The desired reaction is:

“Wait, this is a German bookkeeping app?”

The film should feel expensive.

────────────────────────────────────
REPO / SOURCE OF TRUTH
────────────────────────────────────

First inspect the real repositories before designing anything.

Main product:
  /taxtello/main

Existing Remotion project:
  /taxtello/beta-motion

Important real brand sources:

  /taxtello/main/public/css/app/_00-tokens.css
  /taxtello/main/docs/design/TOKENS.md
  /taxtello/main/public/taxtello-wordmark.png
  /taxtello/main/public/icons.svg

Existing current product screenshots can be found under:

  /taxtello/main/artifacts/smoke-ui-smoke/

Prefer the newest valid screenshots/current source over stale artifacts.

There is already an existing 24-second Remotion hero animation in
/taxtello/beta-motion.

DO NOT replace it.
DO NOT regress it.
DO NOT force its current AI-connections storyline into this new film.

Create a new independent composition for this task, e.g.

  TaxtelloShowreel15

You may reuse good infrastructure, fonts, rendering utilities, motion primitives,
easing curves, asset loading and QA infrastructure from beta-motion where useful.

But creatively this should be a new film.

Before implementation, inspect the actual Taxtello UI and understand the product.

Do not invent functionality that does not exist.

────────────────────────────────────
REAL TAXTELLO VISUAL LANGUAGE
────────────────────────────────────

Use the real design system.

Core palette:

Background:
  #0c0f1a

Elevated surfaces:
  #111525
  #131722
  #1a2032

Primary brand gold:
  #e8b84b

Gold highlight:
  #f5d07a

Gold depth:
  #9b6d18

Primary text:
  #e8eaf2

Strong warm white:
  #f6f4eb

Secondary text:
  #8b93b5

Positive:
  #34d399

Negative/error only where semantically necessary:
  #f87171

Typography:
  Plus Jakarta Sans

Numbers / financial values where appropriate:
  JetBrains Mono

Use the actual Taxtello wordmark and/or Taxtello mark.
Do not redraw or approximate the logo.

Taxtello's gold should feel like a precious accent, not a yellow UI flood.

Think:
dark metal
warm gold
glass
ink
precision
quiet confidence

NOT:
cyberpunk
crypto
neon
gaming
generic AI purple
rainbow gradients

────────────────────────────────────
CORE CREATIVE RULES
────────────────────────────────────

Follow these rules ruthlessly:

1. ONE SHOT = ONE IDEA.

2. Every scene needs room to breathe.

3. The product UI is the hero.

4. Do not plaster explanatory copy everywhere.

5. Do not use hard cuts unless there is a deliberate reason.

6. Prefer object-driven transitions:
   a card becomes the next card,
   a chart line becomes a connector,
   a receipt becomes a booking,
   a number becomes another interface element,
   the camera moves through the product.

7. Use premium easing.
   No linear movement.

8. Motion should overlap naturally.
   Elements should not all start and stop at exactly the same frame.

9. Use depth sparingly:
   perspective,
   soft parallax,
   scale,
   foreground/background separation,
   controlled depth of field if achievable.

10. NO effect exists simply because it looks cool.

11. No particle spam.

12. No fake glassmorphism everywhere.

13. No excessive blur.

14. No pointless 3D spinning cards.

15. No constant zooming.

16. No 20 different animation styles.

17. No bouncing UI.

18. No giant marketing paragraph.

19. Do not imitate a particular Apple commercial shot-for-shot.
    Capture the philosophy and production quality instead.

The visual confidence should come from restraint.

────────────────────────────────────
FORMAT
────────────────────────────────────

Primary master:

1920 × 1080
60 fps
16:9
H.264
maximum duration: 15.0 seconds

Target runtime:
approximately 14.0–15.0 seconds.

It must work as a social-media product reveal even without sound.

If practical AFTER the master is finished, also create a deliberately recomposed
vertical/social variant.

Do not merely crop the desktop composition.

But the desktop master is the priority.

────────────────────────────────────
STORY / EMOTIONAL ARC
────────────────────────────────────

Do not make this a list of five features.

It should feel like one continuous thought:

CHAOS → CONTROL → CLARITY → TAXTELLO

The first 1.5 seconds must already look premium.

The first meaningful product moment should happen by ~2 seconds.

No five-second logo intro.

Possible narrative direction:

“Everything about your business, finally in one place.”

But SHOW this instead of explaining it.

I want approximately four visual ideas across the whole film.

Use the strongest REAL Taxtello surfaces you find in the repository.

Strong candidates include:

• Finanzcockpit / Dashboard
• Rechnungen
• Belege
• Bank / matching
• Steuergesundheit / tax overview

You do NOT need to show all of them.

Choose the visually strongest combination.

────────────────────────────────────
SUGGESTED 15-SECOND STORYBOARD
────────────────────────────────────

Treat this as a strong starting point, not a rigid template.

0.00 – 1.20

BLACK / NAVY.

A tiny warm-gold glint appears.

The glint elegantly reveals either the Taxtello mark or a fragment of the
wordmark.

No generic logo fade.

Think machined precision.

The camera moves through or past the mark and the UI begins to emerge from it.

Very little or no copy.

─────────────────

1.20 – 4.40

FINANCIAL CONTROL.

Reveal the actual Taxtello Cockpit as a dimensional product surface.

Not just a screenshot placed on screen.

Reconstruct/crop/layer it so individual interface regions can animate.

The hero financial number resolves crisply.
The chart draws in.
Supporting metrics settle slightly later.

Use subtle stagger.

A single line of copy may appear, for example:

  “Alles im Blick.”

or another equally short German phrase if you find something more fitting.

Maximum ~3–4 words.

The interface must remain recognizable as the real product.

─────────────────

4.40 – 7.50

DOCUMENT / BOOKKEEPING TRANSFORMATION.

Use a visual object from the previous scene as the transition.

Example:

A gold chart point expands into the corner of a receipt/card.
The camera follows it.
A receipt/document enters.
Taxtello identifies or organizes it.
The document snaps elegantly into its corresponding booking / financial record.

Use magnetic alignment and precision.

No cheesy scanner laser.

No floating paper tornado.

Possible micro-copy:

  “Belege. Erledigt.”

Only if it improves the scene.

─────────────────

7.50 – 10.70

MONEY / INVOICES.

Morph or transition naturally into the real Rechnungen interface.

Use one strong moment:

an invoice status changes,
a payment resolves,
an amount moves into place,
or the overview assembles itself.

Numbers should feel tactile and precise.

Use JetBrains Mono where this matches the actual product.

Gold highlights the active state.

Green is used only for a genuinely positive semantic state.

Potential copy:

  “Geld. Im Griff.”

Again: optional and extremely short.

─────────────────

10.70 – 12.80

TAX / CLARITY.

Transition into the real Taxtello tax-health / financial guidance surface.

Do not claim that Taxtello magically guarantees correct taxes.

Communicate visibility and control.

Example:

multiple noisy signals collapse into one calm, structured tax overview.

Potential copy:

  “Steuern im Blick.”

This scene should feel calmer than the previous scene.

The rhythm briefly slows.

─────────────────

12.80 – 15.00

BRAND PAYOFF.

Pull the camera outward.

The UI compresses or folds into one beautiful Taxtello product object / surface.

Darkness returns around it.

The gold Taxtello wordmark resolves.

One short brand line underneath.

Explore strong final lines such as:

  “Dein Business. Klar.”

  “Buchhaltung. Unter Kontrolle.”

  “Einfach mehr Überblick.”

  “Alles fürs Business. An einem Ort.”

Choose based on the actual product positioning you find in the repo.

Do not use a line simply because I suggested it.

The final frame must have enough stillness to register.

End confidently.

No giant bouncing CTA.

────────────────────────────────────
TRANSITIONS
────────────────────────────────────

This is one of the most important parts.

I want transitions that make the viewer think:

“Of course the next scene came from that.”

Good:

chart line → document edge
gold pill → invoice button
financial number → amount in invoice
card edge → next surface
camera push through interface element
shared geometry
mask reveal using actual product shapes

Bad:

crossfade
random wipe
spin transition
glitch
whip-pan every two seconds
generic SaaS slide-left
zoom-blur spam

Direct cuts are allowed only when a deliberate rhythmic impact benefits the film.

────────────────────────────────────
MOTION
────────────────────────────────────

Motion needs weight.

Use curves comparable to:

cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)

where appropriate.

Different elements should have subtly different arrival times.

Prefer:

anticipation
overshoot below ~2%
settling
motion continuation
shared velocity between scenes

Avoid cartoon springiness.

Camera movement should feel like a high-end macro product shoot.

Imagine we are filming a physical premium object even though it is software.

────────────────────────────────────
LIGHTING / MATERIAL
────────────────────────────────────

Use extremely subtle environmental lighting.

Possible treatments:

• soft gold rim lighting
• dark navy falloff
• faint ambient bloom
• soft specular highlight passing across a surface
• restrained vignette
• subtle grain if it materially helps

Keep the interface crisp.

Do NOT blur the product just to look cinematic.

No fake glossy reflections that destroy legibility.

────────────────────────────────────
TYPOGRAPHY
────────────────────────────────────

Use very little copy.

No sentence should compete with the product.

Headlines should generally fit on one line.

Use Plus Jakarta Sans.

Strong typography may occasionally scale very large and become a transition
device itself.

Avoid generic motion-graphics behavior where every word animates independently.

Typography should move as designed objects.

────────────────────────────────────
SOUND / RHYTHM
────────────────────────────────────

Design the motion as if it were cut to approximately 115–120 BPM:
premium, kinetic, sophisticated, not frantic.

Important moments should land musically.

Suggested sound language:

• low soft impact for major reveal
• restrained tactile UI clicks
• subtle metallic/glass tonal tick
• soft low-frequency movement during camera transitions
• elegant resolved tone at the logo payoff

Avoid:

• huge cinematic trailer boom
• EDM risers
• loud whooshes everywhere
• stock “tech interface” sounds
• rap beat
• aggressive bass

If there is no legally safe music/audio asset in the project, DO NOT pull
copyrighted audio from the internet.

Deliver the visual master without copyrighted music and create a concise cue
sheet describing where music/SFX should hit.

If suitable safe/local audio exists, use it.

────────────────────────────────────
REAL PRODUCT ONLY
────────────────────────────────────

videos.prompt:
I WAS QUOTED $3000 FOR THIS!!!

So I asked Opus 5.5 (medium) to create a launch video using Motion Graphics for us.

here's the prompt that one-shots it:

"Create a 15s motion-graphics film explaining {{PRODUCT}}. HyperFrames + GSAP, no voiceover, no footage.
Style: paper-light canvas, marker notes that draw on, real physics, huge kinetic type,
hard light/dark switches, a new idea every 1.5–2 s, a sound on every hit.

COPY: read {{POSITIONING_DOCS}} first. {{ONE_LINER}} For {{AUDIENCE}}. {{WHAT_IT_DOES}}
Name what the product learns, never the abstraction.

RULES
- No chrome (scrubber, timecode, fps, headers). No animator jargon on screen
  ("squash", "stagger", "easing"...). Every word speaks to the buyer.
- No invented results: no %, multipliers, customer names or figures.
- Never use: {{BANNED_WORDS}}.
- Logo: real mark {{LOGO_FILE}} + "{{PRODUCT}}" in {{WORDMARK_FONT}}; never a boxed logo file.

CRAFT
- Colours {{COLOR_CANVAS}} / {{COLOR_INK}} / {{COLOR_ACCENT_1}} / {{COLOR_ACCENT_2}}; notes in the
  accents; dark mode = charcoal matching the palette.
- Fonts {{BRAND_FONTS}}; Anton for kinetic type; Caveat handwriting via stroke-dashoffset.
- Real easing, squash/stretch, stagger, overlap, onion skin, smear, follow-through. Check the
  HyperFrames registry first. Set every from-state at t=0 (seek-safe); never cover an exit.
  One primary move per transition; no generic push/slide/rotate-swing.
- Music in sections: drums drop on the dark switch and while the ball is airborne, slam back
  on the type and the logo. SFX: pops, pen scribbles, whooshes, logo sub-hit. CC0 or generated
  only; log sources. Master -14 LUFS, -2 dBTP, re-measured after AAC encode."

videos.author: truenyl
videos.prompt:
Claude Opus 5.5 is absurdly good at 3D.

I reran one of my recent 3D experiments with Claude Opus 5.5.

Same prompt, same references, same real-world scene I had previously built with GPT-6 Astra.

The result was much better than I expected.

Put simply, for this specific use case, Claude Opus 5.5 was a clear win for me.

The biggest differences for me were instruction following and taste.

With the same references, Opus 5.5 got much closer to the Zelda Breath of the Wild-style look I was aiming for.

The layout felt more intentional.

It picked better camera angles.

Asset placement made more sense.

And I spent much less time fixing basic mistakes.

In my Astra version, I had to repeatedly correct things like tree roots not touching the ground, rough geometry being used where proper assets already existed, or objects being placed in ways that just looked wrong.

Opus 5.5 got much more of this right on its own.

The interesting part for me is that I have almost zero real 3D skills.

I mostly give references, look at the result, explain what feels wrong, and keep iterating.

With better instruction following and visual judgment, that loop becomes dramatically easier.

Still plenty to improve, especially indoors.

Next test is whether I can recreate the interior of the house with the same level of quality.

videos.author: HenriToivar
videos.prompt:
Opus 5.5 is an absolute BEAST in creating videos.

I am extremely shocked because my previous attempts with GPT-6 Astra and Grok 4.6 were quite underwhelming, far from production ready video.

The leap here is gigantic.

This is a ZERO shot video.

【作者补充制作说明】
Why Opus 5.5 is so impressive is because it's is not a video generation model. It uses pure code to generate the sound effects, the music. All of the animations are done with CSS/HTML/JS, it doesn't use any video or image assets.

This is extremely useful for creating detailed explainer videos where you need very fine control over the infographics and consistent deterministic output.

The framework I used was hyperframes and narration is done by OpenAI text-to-speech.
videos.title_vi: Video zero-shot Opus 5.5 vượt GPT-6 Astra và Grok

videos.author: l3d1c
videos.prompt:
I made a launch ad for @grouped_news in an hour with Opus 5.5 and Remotion, and I never opened a video editor. I added the voiceover and music with ElevenLabs.

The ad is a React app. It imports my site's CSS tokens and fonts, so it uses the same design system as the site.

I didn't review it by watching renders. It rendered about 20 stills and tiled them into one contact sheet, so I could check a whole cut at a glance before rendering any video.

Captions are measured in the real font and shrink to fit the 9:16 safe zone, so nothing hides under TikTok's buttons. Every cut lands on a 120 BPM grid, which made the music easy to line up.

It's one codebase, so the 30s, 15s and 6s cuts in 16:9 and 9:16 are each a different list of scenes.

My part was saying what felt wrong.
videos.title_vi: Quảng cáo ra mắt Grouped làm trong một giờ bằng Remotion

videos.author: iammukeshm
videos.prompt:
Claude Opus 5.5 is incredible.

I gave it a pretty simple task:

Create a Remotion-based showreel featuring my work as a developer, content creator, and open-source maintainer.

What I wanted was a cool 30-second motion graphic that introduces  me as a developer and content creator.

That was basically it.

Claude went to work for around 20 minutes, writing the Remotion code, putting together the animations, transitions, layouts, and the overall story.

And this is what it produced.

Stunning, right?!

What surprised me most is that this isn't just AI generating a few video clips.

It's AI building the video programmatically.

The entire thing is code.

Which means I can tweak the content, change the animations, swap assets, update numbers, or completely redesign a section - and render it again.

Video generation was one of those things I thought would take AI quite a while to really crack.

Turns out we're already much closer than I expected.

And for developers, tools like Remotion + coding agents open up some seriously interesting possibilities.

Interested in knowing what prompt I used?

Comment "Remotion".

videos.author: tetsu_tetsu333
videos.prompt:
Opus 5.5×Gemini 3.8 Flash TTSやばい

新作SEOツール「コトサーチ」のリリース動画を、ほぼ自動で作ってくれた。
自分がやったのは「ツールへのログイン」と「承認」だけ。

個人的には、画面スクショまで自動で撮ってくれるところが一線を超えた感じ。
(もちろんナレーションも自然すぎてすごい..)

具体的な手順はこんな感じ👇
① Claudeがブラウザでツールにログイン
（ここだけ自分でやった）

② Claudeがアプリを触って、機能仕様書を作成
機能・料金・言っちゃダメな表現まで整理

③ Claudeがツールの画面スクショを撮影
PC・スマホ・パーツ切り出しで38枚

④ Claudeが絵コンテとナレーション原稿を作成

⑤ ClaudeがRemotionで動画を実装
書き出した静止画を自分で見て、文字切れや重なりまで直してくる

⑥ Gemini 3.8 Flash TTSでナレーション音声を生成
声の設定も原稿の入力もClaudeが操作

⑦ Claudeが音声を32フレーズに分解
話した瞬間に画面とテロップが出るよう自動で同期

⑧ BGMはClaudeがコードで作曲
声の下では自動で音量を下げてくれる

⑨ 52秒の動画が完成

ということでSEOツール「コトサーチ」は10月4日に正式リリースです。
キーワードを入れるだけでSEO記事ができて、サイト全体の内部リンクまで整えられます。
明日のリリースをお楽しみにしててください！！！
